recent_approving.title: Municipal Corporation of Delhi, Delhi v. Association of Victims of Uphaar Tragedy & Ors
recent_approving.label: FOLLOWS
recent_approving.speaker: court
recent_approving.sentence: In D.K. Basu vs. Union of India (1997) 1 SCC 416, a Constitution Bench of this Court held that there is no strait jacket formula for computation of damages and we find that there 75 is no uniformity or yardstick followed in awarding damages for violation of fundamental rights.
recent_approving.prev: The yardsticks normally adopted for determining the compensation payable in a private tort claims are not as such applicable when a constitutional court determines the compensation in cases where there is violation of fundamental rights guaranteed to its citizens.
recent_approving.next: In Rudal Shah’s case (supra) this Court used the terminology “Palliative” for measuring the damages and The formula of “Ad hoc” was applied in Sebastian Hongary’s case (supra) the expression used by this Court for determining the monetary compensation was “Exemplary” cost and the formula adopted was “Punitive” .
